# AI surveillance is being supercharged – and it will chill social progress | Bruce Schneier and Jon Penney

## AI surveillance is being supercharged – and it will chill social progress

These systems will soon be able to track our public and private lives. But we can make the policy choices to reject it

I n the near future, [AI](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/artificialintelligenceai)-powered surveillance systems will be able to track everything we do in public, and much of what we do in private. And if we do something wrong – shoplift, litter, jaywalk, you name it – the system will notice, retain it, tie it to your official government record, communicate that fact to you, and provide real-time alerts to any relevant authorities … and maybe also to the general public.

Think of these systems as automated speed cameras, but on steroids. Only they’ll enforce not just speed limits, but any other rule you can imagine. And you won’t receive a ticket weeks later by mail; you’ll be informed about and fined for your violation immediately.

These systems will combine powerful AI, public and private surveillance via real-time facial recognition technology and digital tracking, mass databases and highly personalized enforcement. If deployed at scale, they will have profound chilling effects not just on personal freedoms, but democracy and social progress itself.

China has been developing its surveillance infrastructure [for years](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/07/08/business/china-surveillance-technology.html). The country has over 600 million surveillance cameras, increasingly powered by AI and facial recognition to [enforce](https://www.cnn.com/2025/12/04/china/china-ai-censorship-surveillance-report-intl-hnk) legal and social rules. Take the case of Lao Duan, a Chinese citizen [blacklisted](https://www.npr.org/2018/10/31/662696776/what-its-like-to-be-on-the-blacklist-in-chinas-new-social-credit-system) by the system after he lost his job and was unable to repay a series of loans. When he visited Beijing, the city’s AI surveillance system identified him by his face at a major intersection and displayed his face, name and citizen ID number on a large electronic billboard nearby with a message that he was an untrustworthy person. Similar systems are now being [deployed](https://www.visiontimes.com/2026/05/05/chinas-cameras-catch-minor-offenses-but-miss-missing-persons-french-report-says.html) across China and integrated with its infamous online [monitoring, censorship](https://www.cnn.com/2025/12/04/china/china-ai-censorship-surveillance-report-intl-hnk) and [social credit](https://time.com/collections/davos-2019/5502592/china-social-credit-score/) systems.

AI surveillance is [now](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/pixels/article/2025/09/01/the-discreet-rise-of-facial-recognition-around-the-world_6744911_13.html) being experimented with in [North America](https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2025/04/clearview-ai-immigration-ice-fbi-surveillance-facial-recognition-hoan-ton-that-hal-lambert-trump/), [South America](https://www.alsur.lat/sites/default/files/2025-11/Facial%20recognition%20and%20surveillance-1.pdf), [Europe](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/pixels/article/2025/09/01/the-discreet-rise-of-facial-recognition-around-the-world_6744911_13.html), [Asia](https://www.biometricupdate.com/202510/facial-recognition-strengthens-security-for-asias-expanding-rail-metro-sector-panel) and [Africa](https://www.theafricareport.com/420018/facial-recognition-ai-driven-surveillance-how-china-is-exporting-its-toolkit-to-africa/). According to a new [report](https://notechforice.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Tech-Behind-ICE-Oligarchs-Immigration-Enforcement-and-the-Threat-to-Democracy.pdf), the US Department of Homeland Security is rapidly increasing its use of AI-based surveillance, including facial recognition and the monitoring of social media accounts, to keep tabs on immigrants, dissidents, journalists, legal observers and protesters. While the systems are ostensibly used to maintain security and public safety, the real aim is often social control. Larry Ellison, CEO of Oracle – a powerful tech giant that works closely with the Trump administration – has [said](https://www.theregister.com/software/2024/09/16/oracle-cloud-ai-will-enable-mass-survei...

AI surveillance raises a range of public policy challenges: technical biases, unauditable systems, and inflexible automated law and social rule enforcement that can promote discrimination and undermine transparency, accountability and the rule of law. But we believe the most urgent and long-term impact will be its broader chilling effects.

In a new book, [Chilling Effects: Repression, Conformity, and Power in the Digital Age](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/chilling-effects/22383D541B3BC45C9145E85DA4824E10#fndtn-metrics), Jon Penney explains how surveillance, technology and power can be weaponized to influence behavior at scale. Surveillance, personalization, uncertainty and authority are all key mechanisms to increase the scale and impact of chilling effects. They cause people to self-censor their words and actions, to become more conformist and compliant and thus easier to manage and control. And the effects are additive: the more mechanisms employed, and the more powerful the form, the greater the chill.

Computerization has long allowed data collectors to track our locations, collect lists of whom we communicate with, and monitor our spending habits – unless we use cash. What’s new is an unprecedented fusion of each of these mechanisms, persistent and unrelenting. AI brings an analytical ability [to](https://slate.com/technology/2023/12/ai-mass-spying-internet-surveillance.html) [spy](https://www.schneier.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Schneier-AI-and-Spying.pdf) on the contents of our communications, and to answer sophisticated questions about our whereabouts and activities: actions that previously required human analysts are now automated. The result will be a kind of supercharged societal level of chilling effects where fear, self-censorship and groupthink reign, and dissent, creativity and innovation become increasingly rare.

In this atmosphere of fear and conformity, risky ideas, social activism and self-reinvention – especially by disfavored groups and targeted populations – are also [chilled](https://www.lgbtqnation.com/2026/01/publishers-are-stepping-back-from-lgbtq-books-amid-bans-the-current-gop-president/). This will have long-term [effects](https://www.schneier.com/essays/archives/2018/11/surveillance_kills_f.html) on social progress.

Consider the relatively recent societal normalization of same-sex relationships and the recreational use of marijuana. Over the decades, those ideas slowly progressed from being both immoral and illegal, to moral but still illegal, and finally to both moral and legal. But in order for any of that to happen, there had to be a counterculture that was able to experiment and eventually demonstrate to the world that morality could change over time. To the extent that AI surveillance chills this sort of experimentation in public or in private, social progress becomes impossible.

There are no real historical precursors to this; these technologies are too new. Even the most notorious and large-scale [domestic surveillance program](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-48218827) in US history, the FBI’s [use of](https://nsarchive.gwu.edu/briefing-book/intelligence/2020-06-25/spying-americans-new-release-infamous-huston-plan) wiretapping, physical mail opening, informants and paper index cards to track alleged communists during the 1950s and 1960s, appears genuinely archaic in light of modern AI-enhanced surveillance. So does East Germany’s human-centric surveillance network during the cold war. Only science fiction, from the likes of George Orwell or Aldous Huxley, come close. But even Big Brother’s “[telescreen](https://bookanalysis.com/1984/telescreen/)” feels decidedly mid-20th-century by comparison.

But we need not sit idly. Now that we recognize the danger of AI-enhanced mass surveillance, we can make the policy choices not to implement it. Bans on facial recognition and other forms of identification tech can slow development; robust new privacy and data protections can restrict data tracking and retention; AI regulations can curtail its most invasive uses; and structural reforms can help us scrutinize and break up powerful state/tech cartels that pave the way for technological excesses like AI surveillance.

The chill of AI-powered mass surveillance will suffocate the very foundations of healthy democratic societies. But we can still choose a different path.

- Bruce Schneier is a security technologist who teaches at the Harvard Kennedy School at Harvard University and University of Toronto’s Munk School
- Jon Penney is an associate professor and York research chair in artificial intelligence, data governance, and the law at Osgoode Hall Law School, York University, in Toronto
- [AI (artificial intelligence)](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/artificialintelligenceai)
- [Opinion](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/commentisfree)
- [Surveillance](https://www.theguardian.com/world/surveillance)
- [China](https://www.theguardian.com/world/china)
- [comment](https://www.theguardian.com/tone/comment)

# AI 監控正在被大幅強化，而且將對社會進步造成寒蟬效應 | Bruce Schneier and Jon Penney

## AI 監控正在被大幅強化，而且將對社會進步造成寒蟬效應

這些系統很快就能追蹤我們的公共與私人生活。但我們可以透過政策選擇來拒絕它

在不久的將來，由 [AI](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/artificialintelligenceai) 驅動的監控系統，將能追蹤我們在公共場所的一切行動，以及許多私人生活中的行為。如果我們做錯事，像是順手牽羊、亂丟垃圾、亂穿馬路，或任何你想得到的違規，系統都會注意到、保存紀錄、連結到你的政府正式紀錄，並把這件事通知你，同時即時向相關主管機關發出警示……甚至也可能通知一般大眾。

你可以把這些系統想成自動測速照相機，但功能被大幅強化。只是它們執法的對象不只速限，而是任何你想像得到的規則。而且你不會在幾週後才收到郵寄罰單；你會立刻被告知違規，並立即被開罰。

這些系統會結合強大的 AI、透過即時臉部辨識技術與數位追蹤進行的公私領域監控、大規模資料庫，以及高度個人化的執法。如果大規模部署，它們不只會對個人自由造成深遠的寒蟬效應，也會對民主與社會進步本身造成影響。

中國多年來一直在發展其監控基礎設施。全國已有超過 6 億支監視器，並越來越仰賴 AI 與臉部辨識來[執行](https://www.cnn.com/2025/12/04/china/china-ai-censorship-surveillance-report-intl-hnk)法律與社會規範。以老段為例，這名中國公民在失業後無法償還一連串貸款，因此被系統[列入黑名單](https://www.npr.org/2018/10/31/662696776/what-its-like-to-be-on-the-blacklist-in-chinas-new-social-credit-system)。他到北京時，市內的 AI 監控系統在一處主要路口透過臉部辨識認出他，並在附近大型電子看板上顯示他的臉、姓名與公民身分證號碼，同時標示他是失信者。類似系統如今正被[部署](https://www.visiontimes.com/2026/05/05/chinas-cameras-catch-minor-offenses-but-miss-missing-persons-french-report-says.html)到中國各地，並與其惡名昭彰的網路[監控、審查](https://www.cnn.com/2025/12/04/china/china-ai-censorship-surveillance-report-intl-hnk)與[社會信用](https://time.com/collections/davos-2019/5502592/china-social-credit-score/)系統整合。

[如今](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/pixels/article/2025/09/01/the-discreet-rise-of-facial-recognition-around-the-world_6744911_13.html)，AI 監控正在[北美](https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2025/04/clearview-ai-immigration-ice-fbi-surveillance-facial-recognition-hoan-ton-that-hal-lambert-trump/)、[南美](https://www.alsur.lat/sites/default/files/2025-11/Facial%20recognition%20and%20surveillance-1.pdf)、[歐洲](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/pixels/article/2025/09/01/the-discreet-rise-of-facial-recognition-around-the-world_6744911_13.html)、[亞洲](https://www.biometricupdate.com/202510/facial-recognition-strengthens-security-for-asias-expanding-rail-metro-sector-panel)與[非洲](https://www.theafricareport.com/420018/facial-recognition-ai-driven-surveillance-how-china-is-exporting-its-toolkit-to-africa/)各地被實驗性採用。根據一份新的[報告](https://notechforice.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Tech-Behind-ICE-Oligarchs-Immigration-Enforcement-and-the-Threat-to-Democracy.pdf)，美國國土安全部（Department of Homeland Security）正快速擴大使用 AI 監控，包括臉部辨識與監看社群媒體帳號，用來掌握移民、異議人士、記者、法律觀察員與抗議者的動態。這些系統表面上是為了維護安全與公共安全而使用，但真正目的往往是社會控制。Oracle 執行長 Larry Ellison——這家強大的科技巨頭與川普政府關係密切——曾[表示](https://www.theregister.com/software/2024/09/16/oracle-cloud-ai-will-enable-mass-survei...

AI 監控帶來一連串公共政策挑戰：技術偏誤、無法稽核的系統，以及僵化的自動化法律與社會規則執行，這些都可能助長歧視，並削弱透明度、究責與法治。但我們認為，最迫切且長期的影響，會是它更廣泛的寒蟬效應。

在新書 [《寒蟬效應：數位時代的壓迫、從眾與權力》](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/chilling-effects/22383D541B3BC45C9145E85DA4824E10#fndtn-metrics)中，Jon Penney 說明了監控、科技與權力如何被武器化，用來大規模影響人的行為。監控、個人化、不確定性與權威，都是擴大寒蟬效應規模與影響力的關鍵機制。它們會讓人自我審查自己的言行，變得更加從眾、順服，也因此更容易被管理與控制。而且這些效果會相互疊加：使用的機制越多、形式越強勢，寒意就越深。

電腦化早已讓資料蒐集者能夠追蹤我們的位置、收集我們和誰通訊的名單，並監控我們的消費習慣，除非我們使用現金。新的地方在於，這些機制如今以前所未有的方式融合在一起，持續不斷、毫不間歇。AI 帶來了一種分析能力，能夠[監](https://slate.com/technology/2023/12/ai-mass-spying-internet-surveillance.html)[視](https://www.schneier.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Schneier-AI-and-Spying.pdf)我們的通訊內容，並回答關於我們行蹤與活動的複雜問題：過去需要人類分析師執行的行動，如今都已自動化。結果將是一種在社會層級上被強化的寒蟬效應，讓恐懼、自我審查與群體迷思居於主導地位，而異議、創造力與創新則越來越少見。

在這種恐懼與從眾的氛圍中，具風險的想法、社會倡議，以及自我重塑，尤其是由不受青睞的群體與被鎖定的人群所發起的，也會受到[寒蟬效應](https://www.lgbtqnation.com/2026/01/publishers-are-stepping-back-from-lgbtq-books-amid-bans-the-current-gop-president/)影響。這將對社會進步產生長期[影響](https://www.schneier.com/essays/archives/2018/11/surveillance_kills_f.html)。

想想同性關係與娛樂用大麻在相對近代才逐漸被社會正常看待。幾十年來，這些觀念慢慢從既不道德也非法，走向道德上可接受但仍屬非法，最後才成為既道德也合法。但要讓這一切發生，必須先有一種反文化能夠實驗，並最終向世界證明：道德觀會隨時間改變。只要 AI 監控對這類在公共或私人場域中的實驗造成寒蟬效應，社會進步就會變得不可能。

這在歷史上沒有真正的先例；這些技術太新了。即使是美國史上最惡名昭彰、規模龐大的[國內監控計畫](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-48218827)，也就是 FBI 在 1950、1960 年代為追蹤所謂共產主義者而[運用](https://nsarchive.gwu.edu/briefing-book/intelligence/2020-06-25/spying-americans-new-release-infamous-huston-plan)電話監聽、拆閱實體信件、線民與紙本索引卡，如今在現代 AI 強化監控面前，也顯得真的是老古董。冷戰時期東德以人為核心的監控網絡也是如此。只有喬治・歐威爾或阿道斯・赫胥黎這類科幻作品比較接近。但相較之下，就連老大哥的「[電幕](https://bookanalysis.com/1984/telescreen/)」也明顯帶著 20 世紀中葉的時代感。

但我們不必只是袖手旁觀。既然我們現在已經認識到 AI 強化的大規模監控有多危險，就可以做出不部署它的政策選擇。禁止臉部辨識與其他形式的身分識別技術，可以放慢其發展；強而有力的新隱私與資料保護制度，可以限制資料追蹤與保存；AI 監管可以遏止其最具侵入性的用途；結構性改革則能幫助我們檢視並拆解強大的國家／科技卡特爾，這些卡特爾正為 AI 監控這類技術濫用鋪路。

AI 驅動的大規模監控所帶來的寒意，將會窒息健康民主社會最根本的基礎。但我們仍然可以選擇另一條路。

- Bruce Schneier 是資安科技專家，任教於哈佛大學甘迺迪學院與多倫多大學蒙克學院
- Jon Penney 是多倫多約克大學奧斯古德霍爾法學院副教授，並擔任人工智慧、資料治理與法律領域的約克研究講座
- [AI（人工智慧）](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/artificialintelligenceai)

## AI 監控正在被大幅強化，而且將對社會進步造成寒蟬效應

這些系統很快就能追蹤我們的公共與私人生活。但我們可以透過政策選擇來拒絕它

在不久的將來，由 [AI](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/artificialintelligenceai) 驅動的監控系統，將能追蹤我們在公共場所的一切行動，以及許多私人生活中的行為。如果我們做錯事，像是順手牽羊、亂丟垃圾、亂穿馬路，或任何你想得到的違規，系統都會注意到、保存紀錄、連結到你的政府正式紀錄，並把這件事通知你，同時即時向相關主管機關發出警示……甚至也可能通知一般大眾。

你可以把這些系統想成自動測速照相機，但功能被大幅強化。只是它們執法的對象不只速限，而是任何你想像得到的規則。而且你不會在幾週後才收到郵寄罰單；你會立刻被告知違規，並立即被開罰。

這些系統會結合強大的 AI、透過即時臉部辨識技術與數位追蹤進行的公私領域監控、大規模資料庫，以及高度個人化的執法。如果大規模部署，它們不只會對個人自由造成深遠的寒蟬效應，也會對民主與社會進步本身造成影響。

中國多年來一直在發展其監控基礎設施。全國已有超過 6 億支監視器，並越來越仰賴 AI 與臉部辨識來[執行](https://www.cnn.com/2025/12/04/china/china-ai-censorship-surveillance-report-intl-hnk)法律與社會規範。以老段為例，這名中國公民在失業後無法償還一連串貸款，因此被系統[列入黑名單](https://www.npr.org/2018/10/31/662696776/what-its-like-to-be-on-the-blacklist-in-chinas-new-social-credit-system)。他到北京時，市內的 AI 監控系統在一處主要路口透過臉部辨識認出他，並在附近大型電子看板上顯示他的臉、姓名與公民身分證號碼，同時標示他是失信者。類似系統如今正被[部署](https://www.visiontimes.com/2026/05/05/chinas-cameras-catch-minor-offenses-but-miss-missing-persons-french-report-says.html)到中國各地，並與其惡名昭彰的網路[監控、審查](https://www.cnn.com/2025/12/04/china/china-ai-censorship-surveillance-report-intl-hnk)與[社會信用](https://time.com/collections/davos-2019/5502592/china-social-credit-score/)系統整合。

[如今](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/pixels/article/2025/09/01/the-discreet-rise-of-facial-recognition-around-the-world_6744911_13.html)，AI 監控正在[北美](https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2025/04/clearview-ai-immigration-ice-fbi-surveillance-facial-recognition-hoan-ton-that-hal-lambert-trump/)、[南美](https://www.alsur.lat/sites/default/files/2025-11/Facial%20recognition%20and%20surveillance-1.pdf)、[歐洲](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/pixels/article/2025/09/01/the-discreet-rise-of-facial-recognition-around-the-world_6744911_13.html)、[亞洲](https://www.biometricupdate.com/202510/facial-recognition-strengthens-security-for-asias-expanding-rail-metro-sector-panel)與[非洲](https://www.theafricareport.com/420018/facial-recognition-ai-driven-surveillance-how-china-is-exporting-its-toolkit-to-africa/)各地被實驗性採用。根據一份新的[報告](https://notechforice.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Tech-Behind-ICE-Oligarchs-Immigration-Enforcement-and-the-Threat-to-Democracy.pdf)，美國國土安全部（Department of Homeland Security）正快速擴大使用 AI 監控，包括臉部辨識與監看社群媒體帳號，用來掌握移民、異議人士、記者、法律觀察員與抗議者的動態。這些系統表面上是為了維護安全與公共安全而使用，但真正目的往往是社會控制。Oracle 執行長 Larry Ellison——這家強大的科技巨頭與川普政府關係密切——曾[表示](https://www.theregister.com/software/2024/09/16/oracle-cloud-ai-will-enable-mass-survei...

AI 監控帶來一連串公共政策挑戰：技術偏誤、無法稽核的系統，以及僵化的自動化法律與社會規則執行，這些都可能助長歧視，並削弱透明度、究責與法治。但我們認為，最迫切且長期的影響，會是它更廣泛的寒蟬效應。

在新書 [《寒蟬效應：數位時代的壓迫、從眾與權力》](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/chilling-effects/22383D541B3BC45C9145E85DA4824E10#fndtn-metrics)中，Jon Penney 說明了監控、科技與權力如何被武器化，用來大規模影響人的行為。監控、個人化、不確定性與權威，都是擴大寒蟬效應規模與影響力的關鍵機制。它們會讓人自我審查自己的言行，變得更加從眾、順服，也因此更容易被管理與控制。而且這些效果會相互疊加：使用的機制越多、形式越強勢，寒意就越深。

電腦化早已讓資料蒐集者能夠追蹤我們的位置、收集我們和誰通訊的名單，並監控我們的消費習慣，除非我們使用現金。新的地方在於，這些機制如今以前所未有的方式融合在一起，持續不斷、毫不間歇。AI 帶來了一種分析能力，能夠[監](https://slate.com/technology/2023/12/ai-mass-spying-internet-surveillance.html)[視](https://www.schneier.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Schneier-AI-and-Spying.pdf)我們的通訊內容，並回答關於我們行蹤與活動的複雜問題：過去需要人類分析師執行的行動，如今都已自動化。結果將是一種在社會層級上被強化的寒蟬效應，讓恐懼、自我審查與群體迷思居於主導地位，而異議、創造力與創新則越來越少見。

在這種恐懼與從眾的氛圍中，具風險的想法、社會倡議，以及自我重塑，尤其是由不受青睞的群體與被鎖定的人群所發起的，也會受到[寒蟬效應](https://www.lgbtqnation.com/2026/01/publishers-are-stepping-back-from-lgbtq-books-amid-bans-the-current-gop-president/)影響。這將對社會進步產生長期[影響](https://www.schneier.com/essays/archives/2018/11/surveillance_kills_f.html)。

想想同性關係與娛樂用大麻在相對近代才逐漸被社會正常看待。幾十年來，這些觀念慢慢從既不道德也非法，走向道德上可接受但仍屬非法，最後才成為既道德也合法。但要讓這一切發生，必須先有一種反文化能夠實驗，並最終向世界證明：道德觀會隨時間改變。只要 AI 監控對這類在公共或私人場域中的實驗造成寒蟬效應，社會進步就會變得不可能。

這在歷史上沒有真正的先例；這些技術太新了。即使是美國史上最惡名昭彰、規模龐大的[國內監控計畫](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-48218827)，也就是 FBI 在 1950、1960 年代為追蹤所謂共產主義者而[運用](https://nsarchive.gwu.edu/briefing-book/intelligence/2020-06-25/spying-americans-new-release-infamous-huston-plan)電話監聽、拆閱實體信件、線民與紙本索引卡，如今在現代 AI 強化監控面前，也顯得真的是老古董。冷戰時期東德以人為核心的監控網絡也是如此。只有喬治・歐威爾或阿道斯・赫胥黎這類科幻作品比較接近。但相較之下，就連老大哥的「[電幕](https://bookanalysis.com/1984/telescreen/)」也明顯帶著 20 世紀中葉的時代感。

但我們不必只是袖手旁觀。既然我們現在已經認識到 AI 強化的大規模監控有多危險，就可以做出不部署它的政策選擇。禁止臉部辨識與其他形式的身分識別技術，可以放慢其發展；強而有力的新隱私與資料保護制度，可以限制資料追蹤與保存；AI 監管可以遏止其最具侵入性的用途；結構性改革則能幫助我們檢視並拆解強大的國家／科技卡特爾，這些卡特爾正為 AI 監控這類技術濫用鋪路。

AI 驅動的大規模監控所帶來的寒意，將會窒息健康民主社會最根本的基礎。但我們仍然可以選擇另一條路。
